name: SQuAD 1.1
description: Stanford Question Answering Dataset 1.1 (SQuAD 1.1) is a reading comprehension benchmark with 107,785 questions based on 536 Wikipedia articles. Questions were crowdsourced and answers are text spans from the passage. It was one of the most influential NLP benchmarks of the deep learning era, standardizing the extractive QA task.
typical_sota_score: ~95 F1 (human ~91 F1; models surpassed human in 2018)
reputation: One of the most influential NLP benchmarks ever; introduced at EMNLP 2016; helped launch the MRC research boom; human performance ~91 F1; now saturated
notes: Introduced at EMNLP 2016. First version of SQuAD (later followed by SQuAD 2.0 with unanswerable questions). 107,785 QA pairs over 536 Wikipedia passages. All questions are answerable with a text span. Models trained on SQuAD became pre-training targets for BERT. Now completely saturated - models exceed human performance. Superseded by SQuAD 2.0 for research purposes.
